title: Scaffolded .dev/ hub and Generation 2610 backlog
details: Created .dev/ROADMAP.md, .dev/2610/backlog.json, .dev/2610/ideas.json, and .dev/2610/channels-refactor-plan.md (plan v3, Document First steps 1-3 complete: plan, audit pass 1, owner decisions Q1-Q10 and A1-A3 recorded).

title: Primary email address is never verified
details: Fixed via AUTH-TODO-01: User now implements MustVerifyEmail and verification links are sent. Previously users.email_verified_at was never set by application code, so rank counts (Q2) and the biometric precondition (Q5) could not be met. Audit finding AU-1.

title: Add primary email verification
details: Added signed 24h primary email verification (EmailVerificationController, PrimaryEmailVerification mail, email_verification template) sent on registration and first-run setup, with throttled resend and a profile banner. Google/Apple sign-ins mark the email verified only when the provider confirms that exact address. Verifying recomputes the owners of the member's channels. Covered by EmailVerificationTest.

title: Introduce five-rank model and permission policies
details: Replaced users.role with users.rank (Rank enum, not mass-assignable). Added RankService (Q2 rules, creator excluded from member count), vesper:recompute-ranks scheduled daily 03:00, recomputes on addMember, invite acceptance, member deletion, email verification, channel archive/purge/nuke/expiry. Added UserPolicy, RoomPolicy and accessAdminPanel/viewGeolocation gates; reassigned all 24 isAdmin() call sites and removed isAdmin()/isMember(). Admin II appoint/revoke endpoints list missing prerequisites (AU-9); Admin II cannot delete their last passkey. Covered by RankServiceTest, RankPermissionsTest, AdminTwoAppointmentTest.

title: Add admin audit log with visibility scopes
details: Added admin_audit_logs with AuditAction/AuditVisibility enums and AdminAuditLog::record()/visibleTo(). Records rank changes, Admin II appointment/revocation, and Admin I channel access overrides. Admin I reads all; Admin II reads moderation entries only (AU-8). Reading UI deferred to Phase 7.

title: Channel PINs are stored and compared in plaintext
details: Fixed: Room::pin is now a write-only attribute that stores only a hash in passcode_hash; the migration hashes existing PINs and drops the plaintext column. verifyPasscode checks the hash only. The admin console no longer shows or copies PINs (edit modal: blank keeps the PIN), invitation emails and the direct-invite status message no longer include it. Covered by ChannelManagementTest (no plaintext in the row, PIN still opens, blank PIN kept).

title: Add channel types, member channel creation, and unified entry gate
details: Added ChannelType enum and rooms.type/description/is_system (existing rooms become prs); ChannelAccessService (visibility, entry decision, continued access, 15-minute idle clearance); EnsureChannelClearance middleware on every in-channel route (AU-2, AU-3); member channel creation and creator settings (ChannelController, profile modals); public directory at /directory with limited signed-out details (AU-4); seeded undeletable PRA/PRA-2 system channels (Q8); Admin I audited override kept (Q1); room page heartbeat on real input and pagehide lock (Q10). Private channels are joined only by creation or invitation. Covered by ChannelAccessServiceTest, ChannelClearanceTest, ChannelManagementTest.

title: Retire guest mode and add guest restriction tests
details: Retired guest mode: every channel route requires sign-in and the entry page's register/sign-in forms were removed. Converted the guest cases in GeoLocationTest, SecurityHardeningTest, RoomSecurityTest, PrivacySettingsTest, MessageFlowTest, TacticalFeaturesTest, ProfileAvatarTest and RussianLocalizationTest to signed-in users without removing assertions. Added GuestRestrictionsTest: 20 routes refused with nothing written, sign-in returns to the channel, directory browsable with limited details.

title: Add user tags and server-confirmed mentions
details: Added users.tag (unique, generated from the name on creation and backfilled by migration, editable in the profile with format/reserved/unique validation), UserTagService, member search by tag prefix or name (GET /members/search, public fields only, signed in, throttled) with a profile search panel, and in-channel mentions: messages.index and messages.store return mention_tags = mentioned tags of active members or the creator; the room page highlights only those, outside links and code, as buttons that open the member card (member-profile?tag=, members only). Deviation from plan: highlighting is decided at read time from current membership instead of a message_mentions table written on send, which matches 'highlighted if the tagged user is part of that channel' and needs no table. Formatted messages now pass through DOMPurify 3.2.6 (bundled via resources/js/app.js; lockfile recorded with --lockfile-only and node_modules/dompurify linked to the pnpm global store per the zero-local policy). Covered by UserTagsTest; client formatter logic checked under Node (no browser available).

title: Replace single pin with multi-message pinning
details: Replaced rooms.pinned_message_id with message_pins (existing pins carried over; rollback restores the most recent). A channel holds at most 10 pins, enforced in a transaction. Pinned messages are exempt from every self-destruct path while pinned: the stream query includes them past expires_at, no reader countdown starts, the expiry filter keeps them, text/media are never reported burned, burn-after-reading skips them, and their attachments stay downloadable. Timers resume on unpin. Messages that already self-destructed cannot be pinned. Channel purge still deletes pins. The room page has a collapsible pinned tray (count, latest preview, list with jump and unpin). Pin/unpin remains channel creator and Admin I. The pinned_message (latest) and pinned_message_id response keys are kept for compatibility. Covered by MessagePinningTest; each exemption mutation-checked.

title: Add blocking, kicking, and reporting
details: Added user_blocks, reports and room_user kick columns (kicked_by_user_id, kicked_at). BlockService hides members from each other in both directions, filtered on the server and cached per user: the message feed, reply previews, reactions, the pinned tray, presence, mention highlighting, member search, the member card, email notifications and translation by id; replying to, reacting to and downloading a blocked member's message return 404. A sender's self-destruct timer no longer waits for members who blocked them. Only the channel creator kicks (RoomPolicy::kickMembers, no Admin I override). A kick sets status kicked, is audited (moderation visibility) and recomputes the creator's rank. ChannelAccessService refuses kicked members on entry, on every channel request (mayContinue) and in visibility; invite links, codes, Room::addMember and Admin I direct invites refuse them too. The creator can Allow back a kicked member from a Removed members list on the channel page (status becomes declined, audited as kick_lifted); a private-channel membership that is no longer active also ends a stale session clearance. Block and kick against Admin I/II file a report (origin block_attempt / kick_attempt) and return the same response as a real block or kick (Q3). Admin III (owner decision Q11): blocked and kicked like any member, except that blocks against them do not apply inside channels they created, and blocking them from inside such a channel files a report instead. Members report others by tag with a reason, optional details, channel and message; channels the reporter cannot see are not attached. UI: Block / Report / Remove from channel on the in-channel member card (Block and Remove hidden for members shown as Admin), and a Blocked Members list with Unblock on the profile. Covered by BlockingTest, KickingTest and ReportingTest; 39 guard mutations all killed.

title: Add ban vote system
details: Added ban_cases, ban_votes and users.banned_at with BanVoteService. Admin I or II opens a case by tag or from an open report (the report becomes reviewed); Admin I/II subjects are refused. The subject is restricted at once (EnsureNotRestricted: no posting, reacting, pinning, kicking/allowing back, creating or editing channels, purging, reporting or changing their tag; reading still works) and sees only 'Your account is restricted pending an admin review' (A3). Every other voter is emailed (ban_case_opened template). Voters are Admin I and every Admin II; opening is not a ballot (AU-7) and ballots can be changed until close. vesper:close-ban-cases runs every five minutes and decides cases after 72 hours: strict majority of ballots cast; a tie is decided by Admin I's ballot, or not banned if Admin I did not vote; no ballots = not banned. While no Admin II exists, Admin I's ballot decides at once. Admin I bans an Admin II directly (confirmed, recorded as a closed case). A ban sets banned_at, clears the remember token, deletes passkeys and database sessions; EnsureAccountNotBanned signs a banned member out on any request, whatever the sign-in method. Banned members no longer count toward ranks. Review page at /moderation/bans (Admin I/II; linked from the profile and the admin header) until Phase 7 folds it into the panels. Every step is audited with moderation visibility. Covered by BanVoteTest; 33 of 34 mutants killed, the survivor (> vs >= after a tie check) is equivalent.

title: Build Admin I / II / III panels and channel profile modal
details: AdminPanelScope (Full = Admin I, Global = Admin II, OwnChannels = Admin III) drives one set of admin views; accessAdminPanel now admits every admin rank. AdminDashboardService scopes every query to the viewer: Admin III sees only channels they created, members/invitees/removed members of those channels, and their access logs. Geolocation, IPs, access-log locations, user agents, the network map and GPS sync are Admin I only, stripped in the data layer and hidden in the views (Q9). Admin II/III see hidden profile fields only as members do; the dossier is built per viewer (User::adminDossierFor), emails are hidden from Admin III, full rank labels only for Admin I and the holder. Channel actions authorize via RoomPolicy (edit/archive/notifications/invite links: creator or Admin I; delete: creator or Admin I); direct invitations by user or email, member deletion, console channel creation and email templates are Admin I only (new gates manageMembers, manageEmailTemplates, createConsoleChannels). Channels table gains type, creator, member count and a Profile button; the useless PIN column and +PIN copy button (PINs are write-only since Phase 2) are gone. Channel profile modal (admin.channels.profile, server-rendered and escaped) shows settings, members, pending invitees, open invite links/codes, declined count and removed members; creator IP only for Admin I. Audit log section on the dashboard and logs page (Admin I all, Admin II moderation, Admin III none; AU-8). Admin III keeps the profile as home and reaches the panel from a profile link. 218 new strings (all Gen 2610 UI text plus channel-type labels) translated into the 14 other languages with correct plural forms. Covered by AdminPanelsTest and new ComprehensiveLanguageTest cases; 31 guard mutations killed.

title: Enforce biometric and 2FA entry rules
details: Enforced the biometric precondition (verified primary email plus verified recovery email or confirmed 2FA) on passkey enrollment, with a refusal that lists what is missing. pra now needs a fresh passkey check (WebAuthn assertion bound to the member and the channel, single-use challenge) every time it is opened, for every rank including Admin I; its PIN form is gone. On prs/pus/pra-2, confirmed 2FA keeps PIN-free entry (A1) and members who meet the precondition get a passkey check as an alternative to the PIN instead of the old silent pass. The per-channel switch (room_user.biometric_entry) has a profile toggle and turns both off for that channel. Built on the rewritten, server-verified WebAuthn flow (AUTH-ISSUE-06). Covered by PasskeyEntryTest (35 tests) with a software passkey; 24 guard mutations checked, 2 equivalent survivors (empty-signature short-circuit, missing-challenge TypeError fails closed).

title: Run release gate audits and update documentation
details: Ran the Logic audit (White, Yellow) and Defense audit (Blue, Red) on Gen 2610; ledger entries in .dev/2610/audit-log.json. Findings: ROOT-ISSUE-01 (E2E encryption claim, pending owner wording), ROOT-ISSUE-02 (stale README, fixed), MOD-ISSUE-01 (ban-vote race, fixed), AUTH-ISSUE-07 (no auth rate limits, fixed), MOD-ISSUE-02 (bans cannot be lifted, pending owner decision), MOD-ISSUE-03 (restricted Admin III via admin panel, fixed), MSG-ISSUE-04 (platform-wide card lookup, fixed), MOD-ISSUE-04 (text overflow, fixed), ROOT-ISSUE-03 (local pnpm store, pending owner). Line coverage 85.3% (Xdebug loaded for the run only; no config change). README, CHANGELOG and package.json set to 2610.0.0-bs. The annotated tag v2610.0.0-bs and the GitHub Release are not created yet: they publish, so they wait for owner approval.

title: OAuth callback allowed account takeover with a forged Apple id_token
details: Fixed: the callback never validated the OAuth state, never checked the provider was configured, and trusted an unsigned Apple id_token from the request (readable from the GET query string, which has no CSRF protection). One link signed an attacker in as any user, including Admin I without 2FA. Now: provider must be configured, single-use state is required (hash_equals), Apple identity comes only from the id_token returned by Apple's token endpoint with aud/iss checked. Reproduced first, then covered by OAuthCallbackSecurityTest.

title: Recovery and welcome emails printed unfilled placeholders
details: Fixed: RecoveryEmailVerification passed email/expires_in but its template uses {{recovery_email}}/{{expiry_time}}; MemberWelcomeNotification never passed {{role}}. Both now pass the template's variables (role uses the public rank label). Covered by EmailVerificationTest.

title: Apple sign-in cannot complete its cross-site form_post callback
details: Apple returns via a cross-site POST (response_mode=form_post). The POST callback sits behind CSRF verification and the session cookie is SameSite=lax, so neither the CSRF token nor the stored OAuth state reaches the callback. Apple sign-in was already non-functional before AUTH-ISSUE-03 and remains so. Fix needs a CSRF exemption for the Apple callback plus a state store that survives a cross-site POST (e.g. a short-lived SameSite=None cookie).

title: Any member with channel clearance can permanently destroy the channel
details: Fixed per owner decision (2026-10-16): only the channel creator and Admin I may purge a channel. Added RoomPolicy::destroy, enforced in RoomController::nuke (403 otherwise), and the purge button and modal render only for those users. RoomSecurityTest's nuke test now runs as the creator with all purge assertions kept; new tests prove Admin II, a member, and a guest with clearance are refused and nothing is deleted.

title: Channel radar endpoint exposes peers' IP, ISP, user agent and GPS
details: Fixed per owner decision (2026-10-16): the channel radar is Admin I only. IntelController::radar now requires the viewGeolocation gate (403 otherwise), and the Network Map button renders only for Admin I (it previously showed for any rank displayed as Admin). GeoLocationTest's radar test runs as Admin I; PrivacySettingsTest's peer section now asserts the peer is refused and receives none of the IPs or names, and that Admin I sees both members. The peer masking assertions were replaced because peers can no longer reach the endpoint.

title: Generating an invitation link from the admin console crashed
details: Fixed: AdminController::createInvite called ChannelInvitation::createForRoom() with createdByUser: but the parameter is creator:, so every link/code generation threw an unknown named argument error. The existing test only covered direct user invites. Covered by ChannelManagementTest.

title: Invitation email button linked to #
details: Fixed: ChannelInvitationNotification passed the link as invitation_url, which EmailTemplateService does not use for the button URL, so the 'Enter Secure Channel' button pointed to #. It now also passes channel_url. Covered by ChannelManagementTest.

title: Stored XSS through links in chat messages
details: Fixed: escapeHtml did not escape quotes and the auto-link regex allowed " inside URLs, so a message such as https://x.y/"onmouseover="alert(1)"z produced an <a> with an event handler, letting any channel member run script in other members' browsers. escapeHtml now escapes quotes and formatted messages pass through DOMPurify with a tag/attribute allowlist; the code-copy button moved from an inline onclick to a delegated handler. Verified by running the real formatter under Node.

title: Member card rendered a member's location as HTML
details: Fixed: the in-channel member card set innerHTML from the member's free-text location, allowing stored XSS through the profile location field. The location is now escaped.

title: Replies could quote a message from any channel
details: Fixed: messages.store validated reply_to_id only with exists:messages,id, so a member could reply to a message id from another channel, including a private one they are not in, and the reply preview then showed that message's sender and first 60 characters to everyone in their channel. reply_to_id must now belong to the same channel. Covered by BlockingTest.

title: Stored XSS in the admin member dossier
details: Fixed: openUserDossier wrote the member's free-text profile location into innerHTML, so a member could run script in Admin I's browser by setting a crafted location and waiting for the admin to open their dossier. The location is now built with textContent and language names are escaped. The dossier also no longer receives the full user model (it carried the latest IP, hidden fields and recovery data); it gets User::adminDossierFor($viewer).

title: Changing the primary email kept it marked verified
details: Fixed: ProfileController::update now clears email_verified_at and sends a new verification link when the email changes, and recomputes ranks of channels the member belongs to. Covered by UserTagsTest.

title: @tag autocomplete in the message composer
details: Suggest channel members while typing @ in the composer (desktop input and mobile modal). Not built in Phase 3; members can find tags on member cards and with the profile member search.

title: Translate the UI strings that predate Gen 2610
details: About 240 strings used with __() in views and controllers before the channels refactor have no entry in lang/*.json, so they show in English in every language (for example 'ADMIN CONSOLE', '2FA is not enabled.', ':provider account linked successfully.'). Found while translating the Phase 1-7 strings; out of scope for ADMN-TODO-01. Scan on 2026-10-16: 240 keys used in app/, resources/views/ and routes/ are missing from lang/en.json (including a few added in Phases 5-8). Plan: add them to en.json and translate into the 14 other languages; replace the split JS confirm text on the email templates page with one string. Done 2026-10-16: 256 keys (the 240 older strings plus the new lift-vote strings) added to en.json and translated into the 14 other languages; the email templates page's two-part confirm text is now one string with :count. A scan of app/, resources/views/, routes/ and config/ finds no key missing from en.json.

title: Passkey sign-in never verified the signature
details: Fixed (found while building AUTH-TODO-02): WebAuthnService::verifyLogin looked the credential up by its ID and returned its owner without checking the assertion signature, and skipped the challenge check whenever no challenge was in the session. Anyone who knew a credential ID could sign in as that member. Registration stored the raw attestation object instead of a public key, never required the challenge, and reassigned an existing credential ID to whoever registered it. Rewritten without new dependencies: a small CBOR decoder, COSE (ES256/RS256) to PEM conversion and openssl_verify. Registration and assertion now check the single-use challenge, type, origin, relying-party ID hash, user presence, signature and signature counter; credential IDs cannot be re-registered. Legacy credentials are upgraded on first use from their stored attestation object. Covered by PasskeyEntryTest with a software passkey (tests/Support/FakePasskey).

title: Passkey enrollment from the profile always failed
details: Fixed: the profile page posted the new credential nested under credential/response while WebAuthnController::register validated top-level id/clientDataJSON/attestationObject, so every profile enrollment was refused. The profile client now sends the flat payload and decodes excludeCredentials. All three enrollment clients show the precondition refusal message.

title: Product text claims end-to-end encryption
details: README and the room page described channels as end-to-end encrypted. Messages are encrypted at rest on the server (SafeEncryptedCast) and the server can read them, so the claim overstates the protection. The README wording is corrected in the release commit; the room page string 'End-to-end verified communication via Ghostwire Protocol…' still says it and needs new wording (and retranslation in 15 languages) chosen by the owner.

title: README described an older Vesper
details: Fixed in the release commit: README listed Laravel 12 (the app runs Laravel 13), counted 9 email templates, and did not mention tags, pinning, blocking, kicking, reports, ban votes, the Admin II/III panels or passkey rules.

title: Two admins could open two ban votes about the same member
details: Fixed: BanVoteService::open checked for an open case before its transaction, so two simultaneous requests could both create one. The check now runs inside the transaction after locking the subject's user row. Not reproducible on SQLite in tests (no row locks); covered for the sequential case by BanVoteTest.

title: Sign-in and recovery endpoints had no rate limits
details: Fixed: password sign-in, registration, passkey sign-in (options and verify), the 2FA challenge and the recovery request/reset endpoints accepted unlimited attempts, allowing password and 2FA-code guessing. Throttles added (login, passkey verify, 2FA, reset: 10/min; registration: 5/min; recovery request: 5 per 10 min; passkey options: 20/min). Covered by AuthRateLimitTest.

title: A ban cannot be lifted
details: There is no way to reverse a ban: banned_at stays set, and the member's passkeys and sessions are already gone. A ban decided by mistake (or a direct Admin II ban) is permanent unless someone edits the database. Needs an owner decision: who may lift a ban (Admin I alone, or a vote), and whether it is audited and announced. Owner decision Q13 (2026-10-16): lifting a ban takes a majority vote. Plan: a ban case gains a kind (ban or lift); a lift vote uses the same voters, 72-hour window and tie rules, and the ban stays unless the vote decides to lift it. Fixed 2026-10-16: ban_cases.kind (ban or lift), BanVoteService::openLift, outcomes lifted and upheld, a Banned members list with a lift-vote form on /moderation/bans, ban_lift_opened and ban_lifted emails, and the BanLifted audit action. Covered by the lift-vote tests in BanVoteTest (14 of 14 mutations caught).

title: Members under a ban vote could still act through the admin panel
details: Fixed: EnsureNotRestricted guarded the member-facing routes but not the admin panel, so a restricted Admin III could still purge their channels, change their settings and create invite links from /admin. The admin channel routes are now behind EnsureNotRestricted. Covered by BanVoteTest.

title: The member card looked up anyone on the platform by name
details: Fixed: rooms.member-profile?name= returned the public profile (avatar, age, location, bio as visible to the viewer) of any member with that name, not only people in the channel, so a member could probe for anyone. Lookups by name are now limited to the channel's active members, its creator and its message authors. Six existing card tests enrolled their subject in the channel (fixtures only, assertions unchanged). Covered by UserTagsTest.

title: Long report and ban texts overflowed the review page
details: Fixed: a 1,000-character reason or report with no spaces ran out of its card on /moderation/bans and in the channel profile modal. Those blocks now wrap long words.

title: node_modules holds a local pnpm store
details: node_modules/.pnpm is a full local package store (created 2026-09-05; dompurify was re-linked into it at 14:03 on 2026-10-16 by a pnpm install outside this session), which the JLDN zero-local pnpm policy forbids. Not changed by the audit because it is the owner's working environment; fixing it means re-linking packages from the global store. Cause found 2026-10-16: the project is on the Kingston volume and the pnpm store is on the internal disk, so pnpm cannot hard-link and copies every file (all files have link count 1, 83 MB). Recommendation, tested in a throwaway copy: set enableGlobalVirtualStore: true in a pnpm-workspace.yaml, plus a packageExtensions entry declaring vite as a peer of vite-plugin-full-reload (it imports vite without declaring it). node_modules then holds only symlinks into the global store (about 290 KB), pnpm build succeeds, and the lockfile gains only the peer entry. Waiting for the owner to approve applying it. Applied 2026-10-16 with owner approval: pnpm-workspace.yaml added, node_modules deleted and reinstalled from the global store. node_modules is now 148 KB of links (was 83 MB of copies); pnpm build produces the same bundle and the suite passes.

title: Add Malay as the 16th language
details: Owner request 2026-10-16. Add ms (Bahasa Melayu, flag 🇲🇾) to config/languages.php, a complete lang/ms.json, plural forms (one form, like Indonesian), and location detection for Malaysia and Brunei (Singapore stays English, its working language). Email templates need no files: they are auto-translated per locale from the admin page, which reads the language list from config. Tests that assert 15 languages move to 16. Done 2026-10-16: config entry, complete lang/ms.json (1,136 keys, one plural form), detection for MY and BN by country code, country name and city, and channels whose stored language list covered all 15 earlier languages now allow Malay too. Language tests cover the count, plural form, location detection and a Malay profile page.

title: Translated text in JavaScript shows HTML escape codes
details: Views put translated strings into JavaScript as '{{ __(...) }}'. Blade escapes them for HTML, but text inside a <script> is never HTML-decoded, so an apostrophe or ampersand shows as ' or & in alerts and button labels (for example 26 places in French, Italian, Turkish and Uzbek today, such as 'Verify & Enable 2FA'). Inside an onclick attribute the decoded apostrophe ends the JavaScript string instead. Found while preparing ROOT-TODO-03, which would add more such strings. Fix: whole-string uses in scripts and event attributes become {{ Js::from(__(...)) }}; partial uses are checked one by one. Fixed 2026-10-16: 148 whole-string uses in scripts and event attributes now use Js::from, as do the merged email-template confirm text and the one partial use whose text could show escape codes (the invite copy message). Partial uses inside innerHTML strings already display correctly. Regression test renders the sign-in page in French.

title: Review the machine-translated strings from before Gen 2610
details: Noticed while translating ROOT-TODO-03: some older entries in lang/*.json came from the lang:generate machine translation and use wrong terms, for example passkey as 'Hauptschlüssel' (de), 'Wachtwoord' (nl) and '万能钥匙' (zh), channels as '渠道' (zh), 'Clearance Verified...' as 'Liquidation vérifiée...' (fr), and 'Members' as 'Члены' (ru). Arabic uses حظر for both block and ban, so 'Blocked Members' and 'Banned members' read the same. Needs a pass by a reviewer per language; the new strings use the correct terms.
